edges.mechanism: Proposed CYP3A/P-gp inhibition raising tacrolimus exposure; case of trough 29.9 ng/mL with acute calcineurin-inhibitor nephrotoxicity after high-dose turmeric; Saudi FDA rated turmeric-tacrolimus a probable interaction. A structured 10 g/d turmeric challenge in another transplant recipient showed no level change.
edges.evidence: Case reports plus regulator signal assessment; conflicting; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Curcumin is a potent intestinal BCRP/ABCG2 inhibitor (Ki 0.70 uM); 2 g curcumin increased sulfasalazine AUC 3.2-fold at therapeutic dose.
edges.evidence: Human PK study (n=8)

edges.mechanism: Intestinal BCRP inhibition demonstrated in humans with sulfasalazine; other BCRP substrates may be affected (inferred).
edges.evidence: Human PK study with probe substrate; extrapolation

edges.mechanism: P-gp substrate; curcumin 300 mg/d x6 d lowered talinolol AUC ~33%, whereas 1000 mg/d x14 d raised AUC 80.8% (largest in ABCB1 3435TT).
edges.evidence: Two small human PK studies with opposite results

edges.mechanism: Bidirectional, dose/duration-dependent changes in exposure of the P-gp probe talinolol; modified by ABCB1 genotype.
edges.evidence: Human PK studies; low certainty

edges.mechanism: In vitro inhibition of CYP2C9 (IC50 4.3 uM) and CYP3A4 (16.3 uM), but 4 g curcuminoids + 24 mg piperine did not alter midazolam, flurbiprofen or paracetamol PK in volunteers.
edges.evidence: In vitro positive; short-term human probe study negative

edges.mechanism: Rapamycin is a CYP3A4/P-gp substrate; curcumin inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro and alters P-gp substrate exposure in humans, and a related CYP3A/P-gp substrate (tacrolimus) has case-level interaction reports. No sirolimus-specific study.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic extrapolation; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Turmeric is associated with bleeding risk in patients on anticoagulants; in rats curcumin raised warfarin AUC ~1.6x without PT change.
edges.evidence: Narrative review of case/observational data plus animal PK; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Proposed antiplatelet activity; in rats curcumin raised clopidogrel active-metabolite AUC ~1.6x without change in platelet aggregation.
edges.evidence: Animal PK/PD and review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive bleeding tendency is plausible when turmeric/curcumin is combined with antithrombotic drugs; review links turmeric with bleeding in anticoagulated patients. No aspirin-specific study.
edges.evidence: Review-level evidence; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Curcumin lowers FBG ~4.6-5.9 mg/dL; with glyburide glucose fell further without hypoglycemia.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs plus small open-label study

edges.mechanism: Possible additive modest FBG lowering (curcumin FBG -4.6 mg/dL in MA); no metformin-specific interaction study.
edges.evidence: Inferred from MA; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both lower fasting glucose; additive effect plausible but no combination trial.
edges.evidence: Inferred from curcumin MA only

edges.mechanism: Piperine (in many curcumin products) 20 mg raised phenytoin AUC and Cmax at steady state in epilepsy patients; relevant to narrow-therapeutic-index drugs.
edges.evidence: Human PK study of piperine

edges.mechanism: Curcumin lowers hepcidin and may bind/limit iron absorption; case of iron-deficiency anemia on turmeric extract despite iron supplement, resolving after stopping; mouse data show depleted iron stores.
edges.evidence: Case report, human hepcidin crossover, animal study

edges.mechanism: Both are leading causes of herbal hepatotoxicity and share HLA-B*35:01 as a risk allele; stacking adds DILI exposure.
edges.evidence: Case series and reviews

edges.mechanism: Both among the most-used potentially hepatotoxic botanicals; additive idiosyncratic DILI exposure.
edges.evidence: Population survey and DILI reviews

edges.mechanism: Duplicate curcuminoid (and often piperine) exposure; turmeric products underlie the reported DILI cases.
edges.evidence: LiverTox and DILIN series

edges.mechanism: Duplicate curcumin exposure when combined with a curcumin-containing combination product; cumulative dose relevant to dose-dependent hepatotoxicity concerns.
edges.evidence: Inferred; Italian cases linked to high-dose high-bioavailability products

edges.mechanism: Idiosyncratic, often hepatocellular DILI with HLA-B*35:01 linkage, rare acute liver failure/death; USP advises consulting a clinician with a history of liver problems; rechallenge caused more severe injury.
edges.evidence: DILIN, Italian and pathology case series; USP review

edges.mechanism: Curcumin contracts the gallbladder dose-dependently (29% at 20 mg to 72% at 80 mg within 2 h).
edges.evidence: Small human ultrasound RCTs; clinical outcomes not studied

edges.mechanism: Hepcidin lowering and iron binding; case of iron-deficiency anemia resolving after stopping turmeric.
edges.evidence: Case report plus mechanistic human/animal data

edges.mechanism: Supplemental turmeric (highly soluble oxalate) raised urinary oxalate; applies to turmeric powder rather than purified curcumin.
edges.evidence: Small crossover study (n=11)

edges.mechanism: Allele frequency 0.45 in turmeric-DILI cases vs ~0.06 in controls; carriers may be at higher risk; testing not validated.
edges.evidence: DILIN case series and case report

edges.mechanism: Physiological (not analytical) changes: hepcidin fell 17-19% and ferritin rose ~7% after 6 g curcuma; marked hyperferritinemia reported in turmeric DILI.
edges.evidence: Human crossover study and case report
